Question: What is the smallest positive odd integer \(n\) such that the product \[ 2^{\frac{1}{7}}2^{\frac{3}{7}}\cdots2^{\frac{2n+1}{7}} \] is greater than \(1000?\) (In the product the denominators of the exponents are all sevens, and the numerators are the successive odd integers from \(1\) to \(2n+1.\))
Solution:
Multiplying powers of two adds their exponents. There are \(n+1\) odd numerators from \(1\) through \(2n+1\), so their arithmetic-progression sum is
\[
1+3+\cdots+(2n+1)
=\frac{(n+1)(1+2n+1)}{2}
=(n+1)^2.
\]
Thus the product is
\[
P_n=2^{(n+1)^2/7}.
\]
Increasing \(n\) adds factors greater than one, so \(P_n\) strictly increases. It therefore suffices to locate the threshold between consecutive eligible odd integers.

For \(n=7\), we have \(64/7<19/2\), giving
\[
P_7=2^{64/7}<2^{19/2}
=512\sqrt2<768<1000.
\]
Here \(\sqrt2<3/2\) follows from \(2<9/4\). Every smaller positive odd integer also fails because the product increases with \(n\).

For the next odd integer, \(n=9\),
\[
P_9=2^{100/7}>2^{10}=1024>1000.
\]
Therefore the smallest positive odd integer is \(\boxed{9}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
